content: {"id": "c540dab2-4103-47f0-8484-6cddce48e666", "role": "user", "content": [{"text": "Hypothetical for the DynamoDB latency skill, no AWS calls. Table admin-config, 3-hour window, 60-second periods. GetItem was called 2 to 6 times per minute; p99 jumped between 4 ms and 90 ms from minute to minute. No other operation was called. The table was created 2 days ago so there is no 7-day baseline. No SystemErrors or throttle events recorded. Is p99 degrading?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}

{"id": "43b921dd-3e61-45a0-a4e0-3e59e4133950", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "No — that swing is most likely sampling noise, not real degradation. A few things point that way:

- **Sample size is too small for p99 to mean anything statistically.** With only 2–6 GetItem calls per minute, CloudWatch's "p99" for that period is computed from 2–6 data points. At that volume, p99 ≈ max(sample), so a single slow call (one cold connection, one GC pause, a brief network hiccup) swings the reported value from ~4 ms to ~90 ms. That's not a shifting distribution — it's percentile math breaking down at low n.
- **No corroborating signal.** No throttling, no SystemErrors, and it's a single operation type (GetItem) with no mix of other calls that could explain variance. If the table were actually under load-related stress, you'd typically see throttle events, SuccessfulRequestLatency spikes correlated with higher request counts, or error-rate movement — none of which is present here.
- **No baseline exists yet.** The table is 2 days old, so there's no 7-day-ago comparison window to confirm whether 90 ms is anomalous relative to this table's own history — you only have the 3-hour window itself to judge against.

What would make this a real degradation signal instead of noise:
- p99 climbing and *staying* elevated across consecutive periods rather than oscillating back to baseline minute-to-minute.
- The same pattern persisting once call volume is higher (more samples per period makes p99 statistically meaningful).
- Any correlated throttle, error, or SuccessfulRequestLatency (average/p50) movement — right now p50-type behavior isn't mentioned as moving, only the sparse p99.

If you want, I can look at whether there's a way to pull p50/average alongside p99 for this table to sanity-check whether the "baseline" latency is also moving, or whether this really is just the p99-with-few-samples artifact.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
